summary:
AUDIT: CAPITAL AND CONTRACT SIZES FOR VARIANT 5 ("Les deux"). All amounts are in USD. EUR = USD / 1.1446 on 2026-07-10.

METHOD
- I re-ran variant 5 exactly as specified: trend.run_vol_targeted with forecast_regime, 84 markets, costs and rolls as in run_backtests. The reproduced Sharpe is 1.17. Positions are expressed as a fraction of capital.
- I took the median and the 90th percentile of |position| over 2023-07-10 → 2026-07-10.
- The spec table was built by hand:
  - 71 tickers were mapped to Carver's pysystemtrade instrumentconfig.csv (fetched from raw GitHub) through carry_inputs_info.csv.
  - Exchange documents found by WebSearch filled the rest.
  - Multipliers are converted to the dataset's quote units:
    - HG, HO, RB, grains, soyoil, livestock, sugar, coffee and cotton are in US cents.
    - FX futures are in US cents, except EC1, which is in USD.
    - JY1 = USD per JPY × 1e4, which gives USDJPY 160.9.
    - XM1 is already a contract value in AUD: 108,862 corresponds to about a 4.9% yield on 100k face with a 6% coupon.
    - STIR are quoted 100 − rate. SOFR 95.88 = 4.12%.
- FX rates come from the dataset's FX futures on 2026-07-10: EUR 1.1446, GBP 1.3399, CHF 1.2455, CAD 0.7086, JPY 0.006216, AUD 0.69445, NZD 0.57755, SEK 0.1038, NOK 0.1022, MXN 0.0569. HKD uses the peg, 1/7.80. Futures prices include forward points, which cause less than 1% error.

PRICE CHECK (last back-adjusted row, 2026-07-10, against the market)
- WTI: 71.41 in the data vs a 71.57 close.
- Gold: 4113.7 vs the LBMA PM fix of 4099.
- JB1: 127.3 is consistent with the 10y JGB at 2.885% on 9 July.
- RX1: 125.55 is consistent with Bund yields around 3.0–3.1%.
- HO: 355 c/gal is consistent with ULSD around $150/bbl in mid-2026. Energy vols are 40–60% and crack spreads very wide.
- Nikkei: 68,810 is consistent with a search snippet of 66.8k on 15 July after a −2.7% day. The source of that snippet is unclear.
- Not independently verified: SGX FTSE Taiwan (4034.5) and GIFT Nifty (24,200).

DATA ISSUES FOUND
- carry_inputs_info maps QS1 (ICE low-sulphur gasoil, 100 t) to Carver's GASOILINE, which is RBOB. That mapping is wrong; the correct code is GASOIL.
- 'MES1 Index' is the ICE MSCI EM contract ($50 per point), not the CME Micro E-mini S&P.
- CUA1 is ambiguous: it could be the NYMEX Chicago Ethanol CU (42,000 gal) or the CBOT ethanol contract (29,000 gal).
- Three ticker stems collide and are distinguished only by suffix: SM1 Index (SMI) vs SM1 Comdty (soymeal); QC1 Index (OMXS30) vs QC1 Comdty (London cocoa); NO1 Index (Nikkei) vs NO1 Curncy (NOK).

A. CONTRACT SIZES
- Smallest contracts range from $2.2k to $321k:
  - Micro corn MZC: $2.2k
  - Micro natural gas MNG: $2.9k
  - Micro wheat: $3.2k
  - Mini OMXS30: $3.3k
  - 1OZ gold: $4.1k
  - Nikkei 225 Micro: $4.3k
  - Micro Euro Stoxx 50 (FSXE): $7.2k
  - Micro WTI (MCL): $7.1k
  - Micro FX: $6.9k–15.6k
  - At the top: SOFR $240k, Euribor $278k, SONIA $321k, SGX Taiwan $161k, SPI 200 $152k, MSCI EM $86k.
- Some standard contracts are huge: JGB $791k, DAX $721k, NQ $601k, GC $411k, ES $381k, SI $301k.
- Holding one smallest contract in every one of the 84 markets already means $5.08M of notional.

B. POSITIONS ARE TINY PER MARKET
Median |position| as a share of capital, 2023-07 → 2026-07:

| Class | Median |position| |
|---|---|
| Equities | 0.9–5.7% (median 3.1%) |
| Bonds | 2.8–30% (median 5.9%) |
| STIR | 45–60% |
| FX | 10–20% (median 12.4%) |
| Energy | 2.5–7.9% |
| Metals | 3.2–11.6% |
| Agriculture | 0.9–6.6% (median 2.5%) |

- The 90th percentile is about 2.5× the median.
- Variant 5 positions are 1.74× those of variant 2, so variant 2 needs 1.74× more capital for the same contract counts.

C. MINIMUM CAPITAL (smallest contract, median position)
Summary across the 84 markets:

| Rule | Median | 75th pct | 90th pct | Max |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ≥1 contract | $0.63M | $1.64M | $3.5M | $7.7M (coffee) |
| ≥4 contracts (Carver's rule) | $2.52M | $6.6M | $14.0M | $30.9M |
| ≥1 contract, standard contracts | $2.08M | | | |

- Carver's AFTS formula (4 × N × σ / (IDM 2.5 × weight × 0.20), σ on 2026-07-10) gives a median of $2.83M. That is about 1.1× the empirical figure, with a range of 0.6–2.8× per market.

Cheapest markets, capital for 1 contract / 4 contracts:

| Market | 1 contract | 4 contracts |
|---|---|---|
| 1OZ gold | 35k | 142k |
| MJY | 52k | 208k |
| M6B | 57k | 226k |
| M6A | 61k | 243k |
| MZC (micro corn) | 62k | 247k |
| SGX iron ore | 98k | 391k |
| Mini OMXS30 | 100k | 400k |
| MNG | 107k | 429k |
| MZW (micro wheat) | 113k | 450k |
| M6E | 121k | 486k |
| Nikkei micro | 159k | 637k |

- Micro CAD would be 35k for 1 contract, but MCD is illiquid. With the standard 6C contract it is 346k.

Most expensive markets (capital for 1 contract): coffee 7.7M, cocoa 6.8M, SGX Taiwan 6.5M, London cocoa 4.8M, SPI 200 4.2M, MSCI EM 4.2M, Gilt 4.2M, gasoil 3.6M, palladium 3.6M, feeder cattle 3.3M, Buxl 3.3M, T-bond 3.2M, robusta 3.1M.

D. TIERS — number of markets with at least 1 / at least 4 contracts at the median position

| Capital | All 84 | Accessible (optimistic) | Strict (66-market universe) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 25k | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 |
| 50k | 2 / 0 | 2 / 0 | 1 / 0 |
| 100k | 7 / 0 | 7 / 0 | 5 / 0 |
| 250k | 20 / 6 | 19 / 6 | 12 / 5 |
| 500k | 32 / 12 | 30 / 11 | 19 / 8 |
| 1M | 54 / 20 | 49 / 19 | 32 / 12 |
| 2M | 69 / 32 | 61 / 30 | 43 / 19 |
| 5M | 81 / 56 | 72 / 50 | 61 / 34 |
| 20M | 84 / 81 | 75 / 72 | 66 / 61 |

- The strict universe excludes:
  - markets that are not accessible or are illiquid: GIFT Nifty, ethanol, MIAX HRS wheat;
  - very thin CME SEK and NOK;
  - Euronext MATIF agriculture, where IBKR coverage is unverified;
  - HKFE, SGX, ASX, MX and Nasdaq-Nordic markets, whose EU-retail KID status I could not confirm.
- In the strict universe it also uses the standard contract wherever the micro is essentially untraded (e.g. MSF, MCD, micro HO and RB, Euronext mini bonds).

What survives in the strict universe (≥1 contract):
- **100k:** M6B, MJY, M6A, 1OZ gold, micro corn.
- **250k:** adds M6E, MXN, FSXE, Nikkei micro, MNG, micro wheat, micro soybeans.
- **500k:** adds Schatz, SOFR, Euribor, mini CAC, MCL, micro copper, CAD.
- **1M:** adds micro US equity indices (ES, RTY, DM), DAX micro, AEX mini, mini TOPIX, TU/FV, SONIA, canola, sugar, cotton, NZD.
- 10-year-and-longer bonds, most softs and livestock, palladium and platinum need more than 2M.

E. INTEGER ROUNDING OF THE FULL 84-MARKET VARIANT 5
Three-year simulation, smallest contracts, trade only when the ideal position is more than 0.75 contract away. Reference: ideal vol 20.7%.

| Capital | Correlation with ideal | Tracking error /yr | Realised vol | Other |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 25k | 0.64 | | 7.7% | |
| 100k | 0.86 | 12.2% | 11.6% | 80% of non-zero ideal positions rounded to 0 |
| 250k | 0.92 | 8.7% | | |
| 500k | 0.95 | 6.6% | | |
| 1M | 0.98 | 4.0% | | |
| 2M | 0.993 | 2.4% | | |
| 5M | 0.998 | 1.2% | | |

- With standard contracts instead: 1M gives correlation 0.91 and tracking error 8.7%; 5M gives 0.993 and 2.5%.
- Turnover with smallest contracts:
  - at 1M: about 5,900 trade sides plus 4,300 roll sides per year (404 open contracts on average);
  - at 100k: 383 trade sides plus 349 roll sides per year.
  - These counts are an input for the cost audit.

F. REALISTIC RETAIL PORTFOLIOS
How they were chosen:
- Greedy selection, round-robin across the 6 risk classes.
- A market is added only if every market already in the set keeps at least m contracts at its median once weights are recomputed (equal per class, equal within class) with Carver's IDM.
- Strict universe only.
- Each set was then back-tested unrounded with the variant 5 logic, 1990-01 → 2026-07, using the same cost model.

| Capital | Set | Markets | Sharpe since 1990 | Sharpe since 2010 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 25k | ≥4 contracts | 3: micro corn, MJY, 1OZ gold | 0.48 | 0.36 |
| 25k | ≥1 contract | 9 | 0.64 | 0.31 |
| 50k | ≥4 contracts | 6: adds Nikkei micro, micro wheat, M6B | 0.46 | 0.34 |
| 50k | ≥1 contract | 12 | 0.72 | |
| 100k | ≥4 contracts | 9: adds MNG, FSXE, M6A | 0.64 | 0.31 |
| 100k | ≥1 contract | 17 | 0.75 | |
| 250k | ≥4 contracts | 14: adds Schatz, SOFR, micro soybeans, mini CAC, M6E | 0.73 | 0.39 |
| 250k | ≥1 contract | 27 | 0.92 | |
| 500k | ≥4 contracts | 19: adds MCL, Euribor, canola, MYM, MXN | 0.81 | 0.47 |
| 500k | ≥1 contract | 33 | 0.97 | |
| 1M | ≥4 contracts | 27 | 0.92 | |
| 1M | ≥1 contract | 43 | 0.94 | |
| 2M | ≥4 contracts | 33 | 0.97 | |
| 5M | ≥4 contracts | 44 | 0.95 | |
| 5M | ≥1 contract | 63 | 0.99 | |
| — | Full 84 markets | 84 | 1.17 | 0.54 (−0.42 since 2023-07) |

- The 3-market set had a −60% maximum drawdown in excess of cash.
- Rounding these subsets costs very little: correlation is at least 0.996 for the ≥4-contract sets, with tracking error of 0.4–1.9%/yr. The cost of a small account is lost diversification, not rounding.
- Caveats on these Sharpes:
  - they are in-sample;
  - the basis-point cost model is optimistic for micros, whose per-contract fees are a larger share of notional;
  - markets were chosen by contract size, not by expected return.
- Carver's dynamic optimisation (AFTS strategy 25) would do better than naive rounding between 100k and 1M. I did not simulate it.

G. MARGIN (rough)
- Estimated initial margin / equity ≈ 0.35 × Σ|position| × σ. The factor k = 0.35 is loosely calibrated on typical exchange margins; the plausible range is 0.3–0.45.
- Full variant 5: median about 21% of capital, 95th percentile 34%, maximum 47%. Small subsets: 10–18%.
- So 65–80% of capital can sit in cash or a money-market fund. Notional exposure averages 8.8× capital, mostly from STIR and short bonds.

H. MARKETS YOU FLAGGED
- **GIFT Nifty:** drop. It has traded on NSE IX in GIFT City since 3 July 2023 and is not on IBKR as far as I can find.
- **Ethanol:** drop. It is a thin, mostly block market with an $81k contract.
- **MIAX HRS wheat:** probably drop. It moved off Globex to MIAX Onyx in 2025, and IBKR routing is uncertain.
- **SGX iron ore:** $9.9k contract and very liquid. 1 contract needs 98k, 4 contracts 391k. Worth keeping if IBKR has a KID for EU retail (unverified).
- **SGX A50:** $15k contract, but 716k for 1 contract.
- **SGX Taiwan:** $161k contract, 6.5M for 1 contract — effectively unholdable.
- **HSCEI:** the mini is $10.3k, 813k for 1 contract. The HSI mini is $31k, 1.87M for 1 contract.
- **Euronext milling wheat:** $12.4k contract, 260k for 1 contract.
- **Euronext rapeseed:** $29.6k contract, 1.75M for 1 contract.
- **ICE canola:** $11k contract, 518k for 1 contract.
- **Robusta:** 3.1M for 1 contract.
- **White sugar:** 1.5M for 1 contract.
- **London cocoa:** 4.8M for 1 contract.
- **OAT:** the Eurex contract is $135k, 2.9M for 1 contract. Euronext's mini OAT (EUR 25k notional, launched 22 Sep 2025) is about $34k, 719k for 1 contract, but its liquidity and IBKR availability are unverified.
- **JGB:** the standard contract is $791k, 6.3M for 1 contract. The mini JGB is $79k (illiquid), 626k for 1 contract.
- **ASX 90-day bills:** $159k contract, 353k for 1 contract; KID unverified.
- **SOFR / Euribor / SONIA:** about 435k / 460k / 598k for 1 contract. All are liquid and accessible.
- **Micro Treasury Yield futures:** a different product — $10 per basis point, quoted in yield, cash-settled. There is no price-based micro 2y/5y/10y note; the only price-based micros are the Micro Ultra 10Y and Micro Ultra Bond (1/10 size, launched March 2024, thin).

I. ACCESS FOR A FRENCH RETAIL CLIENT AT IBKR
- IBKR blocks EEA retail clients from any future without a PRIIPs KID.
- CME, ICE, Eurex, Euronext and JPX publish KIDs. For HKFE, SGX, ASX, MX and Nasdaq Nordic I could not confirm.
- Elective professional status lifts this restriction. It requires 2 of 3 criteria: 10 significant trades per quarter over 4 quarters; a portfolio above EUR 500k; one year in a finance job.

CONCLUSION
- The faithful 84-market variant 5 is an institutional-size system. It needs about USD 5M (≥4 contracts in about two-thirds of markets, rounding tracking error about 1%), and about USD 20M to be comfortable.
- USD 1–2M gives a usable replica with micros (correlation 0.98–0.99, tracking error 2.4–4%/yr), at the price of about 10,000 contract-sides a year.
- Below USD 500k only a reduced portfolio of 9–19 markets is possible: mostly micro FX, micro grains, 1OZ gold, Nikkei micro, Euro Stoxx micro, plus Schatz and SOFR. Its back-tested Sharpe is 0.64–0.81 since 1990 and about 0.3–0.47 since 2010, before the extra per-contract cost of micros.
- At USD 25–50k there are only 3–6 markets with ≥4 contracts: Sharpe about 0.46–0.48 historically, drawdowns of about −55 to −60% in excess of cash.

claims.claim: The faithful 84-market variant 5 is an institutional-size system: ~USD 5M for >=4 contracts in about 2/3 of markets with rounding tracking error ~1%/yr, and ~USD 20M for >=4 contracts in nearly all markets.

At USD 100k no market reaches 4 contracts at its median position, and only 5-7 reach 1 contract (micro FX GBP/JPY/AUD, 1OZ gold, micro corn); naive rounding of the full system tracks the ideal with corr 0.86 and halves realised vol.
claims.evidence: tiers.csv row 100k; rounding_tracking.csv full84_smallest_contract at 100k (corr 0.862, vol 11.6% vs 20.7%, 80% of non-zero positions rounded to 0)

claims.claim: The binding constraint is diversification, not contract size alone: v5 median |position| per market is only ~3% of capital for equities and ~2.5% for agriculture, so even micros (~$4-40k) need $0.2-2M each.

Retail-feasible reduced portfolios (3-19 markets, strict universe) had historical Sharpe 0.46-0.81 (1990-2026) and ~0.31-0.47 since 2010, vs 1.17/0.54 for the full 84-market system; this is before the higher per-contract cost of micros.
claims.evidence: subset_backtests.csv (in-sample re-runs of trend.run_vol_targeted on the subsets, same bp cost model)

claims.claim: Carver's AFTS minimum-capital formula gives similar orders of magnitude (median ratio 1.11x vs the empirical median-position method, range 0.6-2.8x).
Last back-adjusted prices (2026-07-10) are plausible current levels: WTI 71.41 vs 71.57 close, gold 4113.7 vs LBMA 4099, JB1 127.3 consistent with 10y JGB 2.885%.
claims.evidence: farms.com WTI week ending 10 Jul 2026; bernama LBMA fix; adnkronos JGB 9 Jul 2026

claims.evidence: GIFT Nifty moved to NSE IX July 2023 (FPI/NRI brokers); CU is a thin, mostly block market; HRSW migrated to MIAX Onyx 2025 — IBKR support not found

claims.claim: CME Micro Treasury Yield futures ($10 DV01, yield-quoted, cash-settled) are a different product from price-based T-note futures; the only price-based Treasury micros are Micro Ultra 10Y and Micro Ultra Bond (1/10 size, launched 25 Mar 2024).
Estimated initial margin is ~21% of capital (median) for the full system, up to ~47% at peaks, so most capital can stay in cash/money market despite ~8.8x average notional exposure.
